messages:
support-elaine: forwarding thread from customer-mike — customer sees ~300k token gap between their private ledger and our invoice for tenant `acme-inc`. They run the on-prem meter agent (v1.8.3) behind a NAT, rolling update last week. attaching two CSV exports and a short tail of agent logs (see below).

customer-mike: here are the numbers: dashboard shows 1,200,345 tokens (30d), invoice line shows 901,210. We rely on your ledger for billing reconciliation. Happened after your agents were upgraded.

ryan-ops: thanks — can you paste the agent version + uptime and the timeframe where counts diverge? also any recent network interruptions on your side?

customer-mike: agent reports: `redwood-meter-agent v1.8.3+rev-a2`
Uptime: rebooted 2024-08-08T03:12:10Z during our maintenance window (rolling). Discrepancy window: 2024-08-07 22:00 -> 2024-08-08 04:00 UTC. No reported networking outage but we did see high egress NAT queueing.

marco-sre: quick hypothesis: post-upgrade buffering + heartbeat squeeze could have caused reorder or partial drops during high throughput. We sometimes see offline buffer chunks get coalesced and, if a replay fails, the agent marks events as sent but server never ingests duplicates properly -> ledger mismatch. Need logs and the agent's local buffer index.

eng-ml-ana: also check tokenizer/runtime changes between versions — small tokenizer deltas can change token counts. Did you change any tokenization config or the model variant pinned on the host?

platform-joan: ask the customer to run these commands and paste outputs: 
```
journalctl -u redwood-meter-agent --since "2024-08-07 21:30:00" --until "2024-08-08 05:30:00" | sed -n '1,200p'
redwood-meterctl status --agent-dir /var/lib/redwood-meter
ls -l /var/lib/redwood-meter/offline_*
ntpstat || chronyc sources
```
We want: agent logs around flush/replay, files in offline buffer dir, and any stray timestamps.

customer-mike: pasted outputs (trimmed):
`[2024-08-08T02:09:11Z] INFO flush: wrote chunk id=chunk-20240808-0209 size=12345 seq_start=865432 seq_end=866120`
`[2024-08-08T02:09:12Z] WARN replay: http 502 on send, will retry`
`[2024-08-08T02:09:15Z] ERROR replay: replay failed, marking chunk as SENT but received no ack`
`/var/lib/redwood-meter/offline_chunk_20240808_0209 (size 12MB)`
`ntpstat: unsynchronised`

marco-sre: that `marking chunk as SENT` log is suspicious — agent is incorrectly marking chunk state before server ack when it hit a transient 502. I want to run a safe replay from the customer side to reconstruct ledger rows:

1) snapshot local chunk -> upload to our S3 staging for analysis
2) run `redwood-meterctl replay --tenant=acme-inc --chunk /var/lib/redwood-meter/offline_chunk_20240808_0209 --mode=dryrun --out replay_manifest.json`

If dryrun shows events that did not make it to the ledger, we can compute delta and reconcile invoice.

ryan-ops: assigning to eng-runtime to inspect server-side ack handling for 502 paths; marco, can you reproduce with a local script that simulates transient 502 and a chunk marked SENT prematurely? If yes, we need a hotfix.

marco-sre: I'll try reproduce. Also flagging this as a possible clock-skew issue — `ntpstat` unsynchronised means timestamps on events could be out of order causing dedupe logic to drop or mis-apply entries. Ask the customer to enable NTP/chrony and restart the agent and then run a controlled replay of the affected window.

eng-ml-ana: to address tokenization differences: request a sample of raw request payload (prompt + model name + tokenizer metadata) from the audit log for a few records in the window. If the agent used a different tokenizer binary after upgrade, counts could differ by a few percent. But 25% gap looks more like missing events rather than tokenization.

platform-joan: I've created a temporary support bucket and sent `s3://redwood-support-acme-2024/replay/` write creds to customer-mike via DM. Please upload the chunk and the replay_manifest.json. We'll run compute_delta on our side.

billing-bot: noticed invoice `inv-2024-08-acme` has been flagged for manual review. Please include the replay_manifest when requesting adjustment.

customer-mike: uploaded chunk and replay manifest to the support bucket. Manifest (excerpt): `{\n  "chunk_id": "chunk-20240808-0209",\n  "events": 688,\n  "detected_missing": 212\n}`

marco-sre: good. On our end `redwood-replay-analyzer` shows ~212 events in that chunk were never applied to ledger due to the 502+mark-sent path. We'll open a billing reconciliation and propose credit for the missing events. Root cause: agent marks chunk SENT before ack on certain transient failures + unsynced system clock complicating dedupe.

ryan-ops: follow-ups: 
- eng-runtime: patch agent to only mark SENT after receiving ack OR after deterministic retry exhaustion (work item).
- platform: add a healthcheck rule that alerts when `ntpstat` unsynchronized on private agents.
- support: coordinate billing credit request and notify customer timeline.

support-elaine: noted. I've opened ticket SUP-2024-9883 and added all artifacts. Customer requested ETA for credit — can we get tentative amount?

billing-bot: provisional credit calc attached to ticket: 212 missing events -> escrows to ~215k tokens -> $64.78 provisional credit pending engineering confirmation.

marco-sre: I'll draft a short postmortem and the minimal agent patch (v1.8.4) that fixes the SENT state race. Will include repro script and test harness. Will also add an integration test that simulates 502 on first POST then 200 on retry to assert chunk lifecycle.

customer-mike: appreciate the quick response. Please keep us posted.

support-elaine: will update ticket and ping when billing adjustment done. :thumbsup:
